instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toast the bread slices, then soak them in a bowl of water for a minute and squeeze them out hard. Tear them into small pieces in a large bowl.

Grate the onion into the bowl. Mince 2 of the garlic cloves and chop 1/2 cup of the parsley. Add them to the bowl with the beef, the egg, the cumin, the paprika, the black pepper and 1 tsp of the salt.
Mix with your hands until it holds together. Stop as soon as there are no streaks left. Any longer and the meatballs come out dense.
Slice the potatoes 1/2 inch thick. Toss them in a bowl with 1/2 tsp of the salt. Lay them in a 9 by 13 inch baking dish in overlapping rows.
Shape the meat into about 16 meatballs, a little less than the size of a golf ball. Flatten each one slightly and set one on each potato slice.
Meanwhile, slice the peppers into rings and halve the cherry tomatoes. Scatter them over the meatballs with the last garlic clove, minced, and 2 tbsp of the parsley. Dot the butter over the top.
In a small bowl, stir the tomato sauce with 1/4 cup water and the last 1/2 tsp salt. Pour it over the dish.
Cover the dish with parchment, then with foil. Bake for 45 minutes.

Take off the foil and parchment. Bake for 25 minutes, until the potatoes are soft and the edges of the meatballs are browned. You're cooking the meatballs to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink left.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Sprinkle the rest of the parsley over the top and serve from the dish. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: Cup of Yum (4.9 from 22 ratings, read from the visible rating) leads. It layers a potato slice, a meatball, then peppers, tomato, garlic and parsley, covers the dish for 55 minutes at 450°F and uncovers it for 20. In the Kitchen with April (no rating shown) bakes the same layers at a lower heat in a thinner tomato sauce. Pomona uses 425°F, a full can of tomato sauce, a fixed 70 minutes, and a meatball mix from the April version since Cup of Yum's lives on another page.
